items.title: Pay 'import duties' to release parcel (suspected scam)
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date, not a period to count. As printed: pay by 09.11.2026. This date is only 4 calendar days after the letter's own date (05.11.2026), an unusually short and pressuring deadline typical of parcel/customs scam letters.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a parcel/customs scam: German customs (Zoll) never collects import VAT or duties via bank transfer to a named private company — it is handled through the carrier (e.g. DHL, Deutsche Post) or the official Zollamt/Bundeskasse, never 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.'

The payment IBAN (DE96 7001 0080 0661 2345 67) belongs to 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.', a private company whose name does not match the sender 'Paketzentrum Musterstadt – Zollabwicklung' — a classic mismatch between sender and payee.
The sender's email domain 'clearance-mail.example' is a placeholder/example domain, not a real registered company or postal-service domain — this strongly suggests a fake sender.

The letter insists on contact 'ausschließlich per WhatsApp' and gives no verifiable company registration, postal tracking link, or official customs reference — legitimate German customs and parcel services do not restrict contact to WhatsApp only.
The very short 4-day payment deadline combined with a threat to destroy or return the goods is a pressure tactic commonly used in scam letters to prevent the recipient from checking the claim.
Do not pay this invoice or share any personal/banking details; verify any real parcel via the actual carrier's official tracking and the official Zoll (customs) website before taking any action.
